title: Private offline bundles: key rotation + trust store update guide (air-gapped)
author: Kira Thompson
description: Summary: Adds customer-facing documentation for signing key rotation and trust store updates for Redwood Private offline bundles in air-gapped environments. This explains (1) how rotations are announced and staged (overlap window with multiple trusted keys), (2) how customers update trust roots offline (via a trust store update package or manual key file update, depending on deployment), and (3) what Support expects when troubleshooting unknown-key and post-rotation verification failures. Motivation: Pilot customers asked for a single canonical reference that answers “what changes on rotation?”, “what do I need to copy into the air-gap?”, and “how do I prove my installer trusts the new key before attempting an upgrade?”. This PR aligns language with installer behavior (fail-closed on unknown key; break-glass requires explicit policy gating and produces audit markers) and with Release Eng’s rotation cadence guidance. Scope: Docs only (no product changes). References: Linear ENG-4825 (trust store / rotation), ENG-4850 (docs + runbooks), PM-894 (GA criteria). Also addresses recurring Support case patterns (SUP-31910: unknown signing key after rotation). Content highlights: - Defines terms: signing key, trust store, key set ID, overlap window, “active signing key” vs “trusted verification key set”. - Rotation lifecycle: announce -> publish trust store update -> overlap window -> switch signing key -> retire old key after minimum window. - Air-gapped update flow: verify checksum/signature of the trust update package out-of-band, transfer via approved media, apply update to installer trust store, verify with `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --verify` before running upgrade. - Failure handling: clear guidance for error `RWPB-VERIFY-UNK-KEY` (unknown key) and `RWPB-VERIFY-NOTYETVALID` (time skew); includes what logs and commands to collect. - Support expectations: attach `bundle inspect` output, trust store version, installer version, and support bundle (includes verification metadata) where permitted. Review notes: Includes a small FAQ and a one-page runbook excerpt for SE/Support (kept within the Private docs section).
